title: sliding-cutoff length-fusion batcher: dynamic cutoff and greedy coalescer to reduce tail padding
author: Aisha Patel
description: Background and motivation: production traces show persistent tail padding inefficiency when a small number of very short requests interleave with a long-running cohort, which inflates per-token cost and increases kernel launch overhead on multi-tenant queues. This PR introduces the 'sliding-cutoff length-fusion batcher', a hybrid heuristic that combines a dynamically-updated length cutoff with a greedy fusion pass to coalesce close-length requests into a fusion slot. Goals: reduce padding overhead for mixed-length workloads, preserve latency SLOs for short requests, and keep admission logic cheap for the hot path. Key ideas: 1) Maintain a lightweight moving-statistics window per-slot that estimates 90th/median seqlen distribution; 2) Compute a sliding cutoff T such that requests with length <= T are eligible to be fused into short slots while longer requests are routed to long slots; 3) Greedy fusion: within a short-slot, allow limited fusion of one long request if combined padding cost is below a configurable threshold; 4) Integrate with KV-cache prefill: when a fusion includes a long request, prefetch its KV slices ahead-of-time to avoid stall when fused into an ongoing short slot. Implementation summary: - runtime/batching/sliding_cutoff.py: new coordinator implementing per-slot moving windows (exponential EWMA) and sliding cutoff computation; admission APIs for is_eligible(request, slot) and try_fuse(request, slot). - runtime/batching/fusion_policy.py: fusion cost model and configurable thresholds, unit-tested. - runtime/serve/slot_coordinator.py: hook points where the batch scheduler consults the sliding-cutoff coordinator before enqueuing/fusing. - runtime/kv/prefetcher.py: small opt-in prefetch path to pre-populate KV-cache for fused long requests; guarded behind a feature flag. - tests/runtime/batching/test_sliding_cutoff.py and integration tests under tests/integration/batching/cover_mixed_lengths.py. Performance impact: on our internal mixed-workload harness (50% short < 32 tokens, 30% mid 32-256, 20% long > 1024) we observed a 12-18% reduction in average pad-tokens-per-request and a 6-10% improvement in avg tokens/sec normalized for identical GPU allocation. Tail latency p95 for short requests improved by ~8-12ms in heavy load scenarios due to avoidance of long-slot head-of-line blocking. Backwards compatibility and rollout: the feature is behind a runtime flag 'enable_sliding_cutoff_fusion' and defaulted-off for dedicated customers until 2 weeks of canary telemetry. The config surface includes: sliding_window_alpha, cutoff_percentile (default 90), fusion_cost_threshold, kv_prefetch_enabled (default false), and max_fusion_long_rate (safeguard against too many long fusions). Checklist: - [x] design doc (Linear ENG-2394) and microbenchmarks - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] feature-flag gating and telemetry hooks - [x] docs: short note in Batching Guide - [x] observability: added metrics for cutoff T per-slot and fusion decisions - [x] rollout plan attached to ENG-2411 Changeset summary: see commits list below. Related work: differs from bucketing/quantile approaches by keeping per-slot learned thresholds and allowing opportunistic fusion (rather than rigid buckets). This keeps scheduling cheap and adapts quickly to workload shifts. Caveats: in synthetic pathological patterns (bursty long-only tail) aggressive fusion can increase KV pressure; we protect against that via kv_prefetch_enabled=false default and by sampling-based backpressure metrics.

review_thread: Miguel Santos: Nice approach, Aisha. Two questions: 1) how expensive is the per-slot EWMA in high-slot-count setups? 2) can you show a microbenchmark that isolates kernel launch overhead improvements?

Aisha Patel: EWMA is constant per slot (2 flops per update) and we keep the update in the scheduler hot-path with an inlined fast-path; added a microbenchmark commit that measures kernel-launch rate and pad-token stats. See commit b2c9e51.

Jingwei Zhao: Looks good overall. Please add a safety cap so that cutoff never goes below min_eligible_token (to avoid starving mids). Also request: emit a gauge metric for sampled fusion cost so we can tune the threshold without re-deploying.
Aisha Patel: Added min_eligible_token (config) and a fusion_cost_sample metric in c3d0a8f. Also added a test which verifies cutoff clamp behavior.
Oliver Grant: Approving after a couple nits in doc wording and renaming 'kv_prefetch_enabled' to be explicit in console UI. Please squash and rebase on latest main.
Aisha Patel: Addressed doc wording and updated flag name to 'enable_kv_prefetch_for_fusion' and rebased. Squash ready.

Rollback: flip feature flags off.
